title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

errors: The system is redundant, as Grothendieck himself notes on the next page: adjacency (4) follows from (7).

The circle claim ('at most two segments with δI={x,y}, exactly two iff circle') is false if lieux at a vertex are points rather than branch-germs: a theta graph with two trivalent vertices gives three segments with the same boundary. It holds only under the germ/half-edge reading plus an implicit axiom that a critical lieu bounds exactly one segment and a non-critical one exactly two. That axiom is not stated on this page.
Axiom E1 (non-disjointness is an equivalence relation) needs reflexivity, so 'x disjoint from x' must be excluded. That exclusion is consistent with 'disjoint implies distinct' in (3).
Item (5) only says specialization implies x critical and y non-critical. Nothing yet ties it to segments, e.g. x ∈ δI and y ∈ Ĩ∖δI. The page is a draft and the data are not yet coherent.

ideas.what: Recursive (on n) purely combinatorial definition of 'forms' of dimension n, i.e. tame topological shapes
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology / combinatorial stratified spaces; o-minimal structures; regular CW complexes; conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Programme announced by Grothendieck in the Esquisse (1984); o-minimal realization by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s–1998); stratified spaces by Whitney, Thom, Mather
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme §5–6 announces the programme; this specific recursive axiomatization is not published

ideas.what: Lieux as local branches (germs) distinct from points; points are classes of the 'non-disjoint' equivalence; several critical lieux over one critical point
ideas.modern_name: Half-edge / flag formalism for graphs; places over singular points (normalization); links of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Arbres, 1977) for edges/orientations; half-edge graphs in Kontsevich–Manin and the ribbon-graph literature
ideas.where_published: Flags/darts implicitly used in Esquisse (dessins, cartes); not in this axiomatic form

ideas.what: Specialization relation between critical and non-critical lieux
ideas.modern_name: Closure/specialization order of a stratification; Alexandrov topology on face poset; exit-path order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), McCord (1966) for finite spaces; MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie for exit paths

ideas.what: Segments with boundary δI and support Ĩ; adjacency defined via segments; question whether S embeds in 𝔓₂(L)×𝔓(L)
ideas.modern_name: Edges of a (multi)graph / 1-cells of a CW complex with attaching data

missed.claim: A recursive axiomatics of tame 'forms' of dimension n, built from combinatorial data (lieux, critical lieux, disjointness, adjacency, specialization, segments), is begun here as the concrete 1986 attempt at the Esquisse's tame topology. It was never completed or published, and the literature followed o-minimality and stratified-space theory instead.
missed.quote: Approche vers une construction récurrente (sur l'entier naturel n) d'une "géométrie des formes de dimension n"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a germ-based, purely combinatorial alternative to o-minimal tame topology. It could be compared with combinatorial models of stratified spaces and exit-path ∞-categories, which are likewise built from germs and specialization data.

missed.claim: Using branch-germs ('several critical lieux define the same critical point') as primitive objects links the half-edge/flag combinatorics of dessins and maps to a general theory of singular 1-dimensional spaces, akin to places over singular points of curves.
missed.quote: plusieurs lieux critiques différents peuvent définir le même point critique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests the dessins/ribbon-graph formalism was meant as dimension 1 of a recursive tame-topology theory. That is a link between Esquisse §2–3 and §5 not usually made explicit.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, very rough draft of an unpublished 1986 axiomatization of the Esquisse's 'géométrie des formes'. It is historically interesting (germ-based lieux, a specialization order, recursion on dimension), but the mathematics on this page is elementary graph/stratification combinatorics, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Item 3 reads '... "x et y sont disjoints", impliquant la relation "x et y sont distincts"', not '[-et-]'.
'(5 jours)' is most likely '(5 Juin)'. The date line '(Juin 86)' appears to have the 6 written over a 5.
Item 5 begins 'Une relation plus fine encore ...', with 'S' or 'plus fine' written above as an insertion. The struck words include 'ensemble de parties de L, appelées ... "segments"'.
Item 6 reads approximately 'Un ensemble S, dont les éléments I, J, ... appelés les "segments"'; the insertion above it is struck through.
The left marginal note reads roughly 'Une modèle de une forme de dim 0 ... (i.e. ensemble discret)' and is partly illegible.
The top-left circled label may be 'Ch I' rather than 'Df I'.
